_about: KrakenD metrics as exposed by the telemetry/opentelemetry Prometheus exporter. GENERATED from a real KrakenD run with every component enabled and traffic through every feature. Names are Prometheus names; otel_name is the instrument. Installations can differ: ALWAYS confirm with list_prometheus_metric_names first.

scrape_labels.job: Prometheus job name (from the scrape config).
scrape_labels.instance: host:port of the KrakenD metrics exporter. One per node.
scrape_labels.app: Optional static label used by the official grafana.com dashboards. Only exists if the user's scrape config adds it.

semantic_conventions.detect: list_prometheus_metric_names: http_server_duration_bucket -> default; http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket -> 1.27. Then use each metric's semconv_1_27.name instead of name when present.

label_meanings.http_route: global/proxy layers: the KrakenD ENDPOINT pattern with :param syntax (/users/:id). Requests that match no endpoint get the status text instead: "404 Not Found", and KrakenD's own /__debug/ and /__echo/ calls show up as "200 OK". backend/http_client layers: the BACKEND url_pattern.
label_meanings.krakend_endpoint_route: backend/http_client layers: the KrakenD endpoint the backend call belongs to.
label_meanings.krakend_endpoint_method: backend/http_client layers: method of the KrakenD endpoint.
label_meanings.http_response_status_code: Status code. Global layer: what the client got. http_client: what the backend returned; "0" = no response (timeout/connection error).
label_meanings.clientname: http_client: duplicate of the backend url_pattern. Ignore.
label_meanings.error: proxy/backend: "true" when the layer returned an error.
label_meanings.canceled: proxy/backend: "true" when the context was canceled.
label_meanings.cb_name: Circuit breaker name ('unnamed' when not set in config). Name your breakers.
label_meanings.count: Circuit breaker counter kind; redundant with the metric name.
label_meanings.pool_name: Redis pool address (host:port), not the configured pool name.
label_meanings.messaging_read_acked: Whether the consumed message was ACKed.
label_meanings.messaging_read_processed: Whether the consumed message was processed.
label_meanings.provider: LLM vendor (openai, anthropic, gemini, mistral, bedrock, alibaba).
label_meanings.model: LLM model name as sent to the vendor.
label_meanings.krakend_backend: Backend url_pattern where the guard ran; empty for endpoint-level guards.

backend-roundtrip.lazy: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

backend-connection.lazy: Registered on the first backend call. Points only appear when a new connection is opened (keep-alive reuses connections).

backend-payload.lazy: Registered on the first backend call.

circuit-breaker.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

redis-pool.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.

messaging.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: db_client_connections_create_time_milliseconds
metrics.meaning: Time to create a new Redis connection (ms).
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The time it took to create a new connection.

metrics.name: db_client_connections_hits
metrics.meaning: Times a free connection was found in the pool (cumulative, exported as gauge: use deriv()/delta(), not rate()).
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The number of times free connection was found in the pool

metrics.name: db_client_connections_idle_max
metrics.meaning: Max idle connections allowed.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The maximum number of idle open connections allowed

metrics.name: db_client_connections_idle_min
metrics.meaning: Min idle connections kept.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The minimum number of idle open connections allowed

metrics.name: db_client_connections_max
metrics.meaning: Max open connections allowed (pool_size).
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The maximum number of open connections allowed

metrics.name: db_client_connections_misses
metrics.meaning: Times no free connection was found and a new one had to be created (cumulative gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The number of times free connection was not found in the pool

metrics.name: db_client_connections_timeouts
metrics.meaning: Timeouts obtaining a connection from the pool (cumulative gauge). Any growth = Redis-backed features (rate limit, quota) degraded.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The number of connection timeouts that have occurred trying to obtain a connection from the pool

metrics.name: db_client_connections_usage
metrics.meaning: Connections currently in each state (state=idle|used). used / max = pool saturation.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The number of connections that are currently in state described by the state attribute

metrics.name: db_client_connections_use_time_milliseconds
metrics.meaning: Time between borrowing and returning a connection (ms), by type=command|pipeline and status=ok|error. Effectively Redis command latency as seen by KrakenD.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The time between borrowing a connection and returning it to the pool.

metrics.name: db_client_connections_waits
metrics.meaning: Times a caller had to wait for a connection (cumulative gauge). Growth = pool too small.
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The number of times a connection was waited for

metrics.name: db_client_connections_waits_duration_nanoseconds
metrics.meaning: Total time spent waiting for connections, in nanoseconds (cumulative gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: redis.connection_pools / redis.clusters (per pool: opentelemetry.disable_metrics=false, default). Used by redis rate limits, quotas, semantic cache.
metrics.help: The total time spent for waiting a connection in nanoseconds

metrics.name: http_client_duration
metrics.meaning: Pure HTTP round trip to the backend (until response headers). Best for 'which backend service is slow' (by server_address) and backend status codes. Status 0 = no response (timeout, connection error).
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

metrics.name: http_client_request_canceled_count_total
metrics.meaning: Backend requests canceled before completion (client went away, sibling failure in an aggregation).
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet. Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.name: http_client_request_dns_duration
metrics.meaning: DNS resolution time for backend calls.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call. Points only appear when a new connection is opened (keep-alive reuses connections).

metrics.name: http_client_request_failed_count_total
metrics.meaning: Backend requests that failed at transport level (connection refused/reset, auth token fetch failure...). A backend 5xx is NOT a failure here.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet. Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.name: http_client_request_get_conn_duration
metrics.meaning: Time to obtain a connection from the pool or dial a new one. High = pool exhaustion or slow connects.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call. Points only appear when a new connection is opened (keep-alive reuses connections).

metrics.name: http_client_request_size_total
metrics.meaning: Request body bytes sent to backends.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

metrics.name: http_client_request_started_count_total
metrics.meaning: Backend requests started. rate() = backend request throughput.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

metrics.name: http_client_request_timedout_count_total
metrics.meaning: Backend requests aborted by KrakenD's timeout.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet. Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.name: http_client_request_tls_duration
metrics.meaning: TLS handshake time to backends. Empty for plain HTTP backends.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call. Points only appear when a new connection is opened (keep-alive reuses connections).

metrics.name: http_client_response_no_content_length_total
metrics.meaning: Backend responses without a Content-Length header (chunked/streamed). Their size only shows in the read_payload metrics.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

metrics.name: http_client_response_read_errors_total
metrics.meaning: Errors while reading backend response bodies (truncated/reset streams).
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call. Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.name: http_client_response_read_size_b_total
metrics.meaning: Total bytes read from backend response bodies. rate() = backend ingress bandwidth.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call.

metrics.name: http_client_response_read_size_hist_b
metrics.meaning: Distribution of bytes read per backend response body.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call.

metrics.name: http_client_response_read_time_seconds_total
metrics.meaning: Cumulative time spent reading backend bodies.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call.

metrics.name: http_client_response_read_time_hist_seconds
metrics.meaning: Distribution of body read time per backend response. Large = big or slow-streaming payloads.
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call.

metrics.name: http_client_response_size
metrics.meaning: Backend response size as declared by Content-Length. Only recorded when the backend sends Content-Length (see no-content-length).
metrics.notes: Registered on the first backend call; absent from a gateway that hasn't proxied anything yet.

metrics.name: http_server_duration
metrics.meaning: End-to-end time per request as seen by the client (router + proxy + backends). THE metric for request rate (_count), error rate (status >= 500), status split and user-facing latency.

metrics.name: http_server_response_size
metrics.meaning: Response body size sent to clients. rate(_sum) = egress bandwidth.

metrics.name: krakend_backend_duration
metrics.meaning: Time per backend call including KrakenD's backend-side processing (decoding, filtering). http_route = backend url_pattern; group by krakend_endpoint_route for the endpoint. error="true" = failed backend call.

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_consecutive_failures
metrics.meaning: Current consecutive failures counted by the breaker (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_consecutive_successes
metrics.meaning: Current consecutive successes (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_requests
metrics.meaning: Requests counted in the current breaker interval (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_total_exclusions
metrics.meaning: Requests excluded from breaker accounting in the current interval (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_total_failures
metrics.meaning: Failures in the current breaker interval (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_errors_total_successes
metrics.meaning: Successes in the current breaker interval (gauge).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_state_close_to_open_total
metrics.meaning: Times a breaker OPENED from closed (started rejecting).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_state_half_to_close_total
metrics.meaning: Successful recoveries (half-open back to closed).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)
metrics.notes: Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.
metrics.verified_name: KrakenD EE 3.0, observed with a circuit breaker recovering

metrics.name: krakend_cb_state_half_to_open_total
metrics.meaning: Failed recovery probes (half-open back to open). Steady growth = backend still down. Count this together with close-to-open for 'times opened'.
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_cb_state_open_to_half_total
metrics.meaning: Times a breaker moved from open to half-open (testing recovery).
metrics.enabled_by: qos/circuit-breaker or qos/circuit-breaker/http on a backend (label cb_name = the breaker's name, 'unnamed' if not set)

metrics.name: krakend_llm_tokens_in_total
metrics.meaning: Input (prompt) tokens consumed, by provider and model. Basis for LLM cost dashboards.

metrics.name: krakend_llm_tokens_out_total
metrics.meaning: Output (completion) tokens, by provider and model.

metrics.name: krakend_llm_tokens_total
metrics.meaning: Total tokens, by provider and model.

metrics.name: krakend_promptguard_check_requests_total
metrics.meaning: Prompt guard evaluations. krakend_promptguard_blocked="true" = blocked prompt. http_route = endpoint; krakend_backend = backend url_pattern (empty when the guard is at endpoint level). Does not say which guard matched.

metrics.name: krakend_proxy_duration
metrics.meaning: Time in the proxy pipe for an endpoint: backend fan-out, merge, manipulations. complete="false" = partial (degraded) aggregated response. No status code label.

metrics.name: messaging_read_ack_duration_seconds
metrics.meaning: Time until a consumed message was ACKed (labels messaging_read_acked / messaging_read_processed).
metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: messaging_read_body_duration_seconds

metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: messaging_read_body_size_bytes
metrics.meaning: Size of messages consumed (Kafka).
metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: messaging_read_failure_count_seconds
metrics.meaning: Failed consumes, as a histogram of how long the failing operation took (seconds). Count failures with _count.
metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).
metrics.notes: Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: messaging_write_body_size_bytes
metrics.meaning: Size of messages published (Kafka).
metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).

metrics.name: messaging_write_failure_count_seconds
metrics.meaning: Failed publishes, as a histogram of how long the failing operation took (seconds). Count failures with _count.
metrics.enabled_by: backend/pubsub/publisher/kafka and backend/pubsub/subscriber/kafka. Generic backend/pubsub/* (NATS, SQS, ...) and backend/amqp/* emit no messaging metrics (KrakenD EE 3.0).
metrics.notes: Only exported after the first occurrence of the event.

metrics.name: websocket_client_connections_count_total
metrics.meaning: Connections KrakenD opened to WebSocket backends (label url_path = backend ws URL).

metrics.name: websocket_client_disconnections_count_b_total
metrics.meaning: Disconnections from WebSocket backends.

metrics.name: websocket_client_request_size_hist_b
metrics.meaning: Size of messages sent to WebSocket backends.

metrics.name: websocket_client_response_size_hist_b

metrics.name: websocket_server_connections_count_b_total
metrics.meaning: Client WebSocket connections accepted by KrakenD. No labels: cannot be split per endpoint.

runtime.meaning: Go runtime and process metrics of each KrakenD node. go_* need go_metrics, process_* need process_metrics. Check each family's type: most go_memstats_* and process_* values are GAUGES (use them as-is, avg_over_time/max_over_time; never rate()); only *_total are counters (rate()); go_gc_duration_seconds is a SUMMARY (quantile label 0..1 = pause quantiles of recent cycles; rate(_count) = GCs/s, rate(_sum) = seconds paused per second).

go_gc_duration_seconds.help: A summary of the wall-time pause (stop-the-world) duration in garbage collection cycles.

go_gc_gogc_percent.help: Heap size target percentage configured by the user, otherwise 100. This value is set by the GOGC environment variable, and the runtime/debug.SetGCPercent function. Sourced from /gc/gogc:percent.

go_gc_gomemlimit_bytes.help: Go runtime memory limit configured by the user, otherwise math.MaxInt64. This value is set by the GOMEMLIMIT environment variable, and the runtime/debug.SetMemoryLimit function. Sourced from /gc/gomemlimit:bytes.

go_goroutines.help: Number of goroutines that currently exist.

go_memstats_alloc_bytes.help: Number of bytes allocated in heap and currently in use. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes.

go_memstats_alloc_bytes_total.help: Total number of bytes allocated in heap until now, even if released already. Equals to /gc/heap/allocs:bytes.

go_memstats_buck_hash_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes used by the profiling bucket hash table. Equals to /memory/classes/profiling/buckets:bytes.

go_memstats_frees_total.help: Total number of heap objects frees. Equals to /gc/heap/frees:objects + /gc/heap/tiny/allocs:objects.

go_memstats_gc_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes used for garbage collection system metadata. Equals to /memory/classes/metadata/other:bytes.

go_memstats_heap_alloc_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes allocated and currently in use, same as go_memstats_alloc_bytes. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes.

go_memstats_heap_idle_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes waiting to be used. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/released:bytes + /memory/classes/heap/free:bytes.

go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes that are in use. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes + /memory/classes/heap/unused:bytes

go_memstats_heap_objects.help: Number of currently allocated objects. Equals to /gc/heap/objects:objects.

go_memstats_heap_released_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes released to OS. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/released:bytes.

go_memstats_heap_sys_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes obtained from system. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/objects:bytes + /memory/classes/heap/unused:bytes + /memory/classes/heap/released:bytes + /memory/classes/heap/free:bytes.

go_memstats_last_gc_time_seconds.help: Number of seconds since 1970 of last garbage collection.

go_memstats_mallocs_total.help: Total number of heap objects allocated, both live and gc-ed. Semantically a counter version for go_memstats_heap_objects gauge. Equals to /gc/heap/allocs:objects + /gc/heap/tiny/allocs:objects.

go_memstats_mcache_inuse_bytes.help: Number of bytes in use by mcache structures. Equals to /memory/classes/metadata/mcache/inuse:bytes.

go_memstats_mcache_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes used for mcache structures obtained from system. Equals to /memory/classes/metadata/mcache/inuse:bytes + /memory/classes/metadata/mcache/free:bytes.

go_memstats_mspan_inuse_bytes.help: Number of bytes in use by mspan structures. Equals to /memory/classes/metadata/mspan/inuse:bytes.

go_memstats_mspan_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes used for mspan structures obtained from system. Equals to /memory/classes/metadata/mspan/inuse:bytes + /memory/classes/metadata/mspan/free:bytes.

go_memstats_next_gc_bytes.help: Number of heap bytes when next garbage collection will take place. Equals to /gc/heap/goal:bytes.

go_memstats_other_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes used for other system allocations. Equals to /memory/classes/other:bytes.

go_memstats_stack_inuse_bytes.help: Number of bytes obtained from system for stack allocator in non-CGO environments. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/stacks:bytes.

go_memstats_stack_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes obtained from system for stack allocator. Equals to /memory/classes/heap/stacks:bytes + /memory/classes/os-stacks:bytes.

go_memstats_sys_bytes.help: Number of bytes obtained from system. Equals to /memory/classes/total:byte.

go_sched_gomaxprocs_threads.help: The current runtime.GOMAXPROCS setting, or the number of operating system threads that can execute user-level Go code simultaneously. Sourced from /sched/gomaxprocs:threads.

process_cpu_seconds_total.help: Total user and system CPU time spent in seconds.

process_max_fds.help: Maximum number of open file descriptors.

process_start_time_seconds.help: Start time of the process since unix epoch in seconds.

process_virtual_memory_max_bytes.help: Maximum amount of virtual memory available in bytes.

process_network_receive_bytes_total.help: Number of bytes received by the process over the network.

process_network_transmit_bytes_total.help: Number of bytes sent by the process over the network.

gotchas: Two naming conventions exist (layers.global.semantic_convention). Default ("") -> http_server_duration, http_client_duration...; "1.27" -> http_server_request_duration_seconds, http_client_request_duration_seconds, *_body_size_bytes, and connection timings get a _seconds suffix. Labels and buckets are identical. Detect which one the user has before writing queries: see each metric's semconv_1_27 field.
Under semconv 1.27, http_client_request_size_total (counter) becomes http_client_request_body_size_bytes (histogram): rate(X_total) -> rate(X_sum).
Under semconv 1.27, http_client_response_no_content_length gets a bytes unit (…_no_content_length_bytes_total) although it counts responses.

Lazy instruments: http_client_* only exist after the first backend call; event-only counters (timeouts, canceled, read errors, failures, cb half-to-close) only appear after the first event. Use `or vector(0)` in stats so panels show 0 instead of 'No data'.

Histogram percentiles are interpolated inside buckets (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.075, 0.1, 0.125, ... s). Layers whose real latencies differ by less than a bucket width get the same p95: compare layers with averages (_sum/_count).
Router rate limit rejections surface as http_server_duration status 503 by default; there is no dedicated rate-limit metric.

Prompt guard blocks return HTTP 500 to the client (KrakenD EE 3.0), so they inflate 5xx error rates. Subtract krakend_promptguard_check_requests_total{krakend_promptguard_blocked="true"} when computing gateway errors for AI endpoints.
Prompt guard only inspected the Responses-API 'input' field against an ai/llm openai v1 backend; a chat-completions 'messages' body passed unchecked.
WebSocket server metrics have no labels (no endpoint, no instance-level split besides scrape labels).

WebSocket connection counters carry a bytes unit by mistake: websocket_server_connections_count_b_total, websocket_*_disconnections_count_b_total (but websocket_client_connections_count_total without _b). Use the names as exposed.
Redis pool hits/misses/waits/timeouts are cumulative values exported as GAUGES: use delta()/deriv() or idelta, not rate().
Redis pool_name is the address (localhost:6379), not the configured connection pool name.
Only Kafka backends emit messaging_* metrics; NATS/SQS/etc. pubsub and AMQP backends only show up in http_server/krakend_* layer metrics.

Requests to KrakenD's own /__debug/ and /__echo/ endpoints are counted with http_route="200 OK" even though they're in the default skip_paths. Exclude http_route=~"[0-9]{3} .*" from per-endpoint views.
